text:
deploy-bot: INCIDENT PAGER: GPU capacity exhaustion in prod-us-east-1 — autoscaler failing to add nodes (ASG/launch-template errors). Queue growth observed. Paging ml_oncall_ree and sre_anna. :rotating_light:
ml_oncall_ree: I'm on it. seeing large spike on gpu-queue from 02:12 UTC, queue length ~11.2k, 95th latency -> throttling.
ml_oncall_ree: dashboard shows token generation 503s for some customers and long tail for others.
sre_anna: looking at cluster-autoscaler logs now. getting errors adding instance: "LaunchTemplate mismatch" and also IAM attach role denied for nodegroup role.
engops_jay: I can hit the autoscaler events: "Failed to launch instance: InvalidLaunchTemplateName.NotFound" then "Instance provisioning timed out". Might be a rollout to LT v7 last night that didn't finish.
support_lina: we have ~18 open support tickets referencing generation failures and slow responses, some enterprise customers experiencing degraded throughput.
ml_oncall_ree: mitigation plan: 1) try manual scale-up of dedicated GPU ASG with known-good launch template 2) route traffic to fallback CPU model for non-latency-critical customers 3) remove taint/add toleration if nodes coming up tainted incorrectly.
product_tom: please PS to customers under active SLAs, prioritize enterprise lanes.
sre_anna: running quick check: `kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep gpu` shows 3 ready GPUs, 6 NotReady (boot pending). Events: `FailedAttachVolume` and `FailedAdmission webhook "node-launch-template"`.
engops_jay: that webhook is our infra-guard validating launch template tags. Seems the new LT v7 is missing the `redwood:gpu=true` tag so autoscaler picks it but webhook rejects.
ml_oncall_ree: ok. I'm going to manually bump ASG desired to +6 using LT v6 which we know works. engops_jay can you confirm v6 id?
engops_jay: LT v6 id `lt-0a5b6c7d`. issuing: `aws autoscaling update-auto-scaling-group --auto-scaling-group-name gpu-prod-asg --launch-template LaunchTemplateId=lt-0a5b6c7d,Version=6 --desired-capacity 9`
infra-bot: Command executed: update-auto-scaling-group for gpu-prod-asg -> requested desired 9.
ml_oncall_ree: thanks. also changing routing: updating proxy rule to send non-enterprise customers to cpu-fallback pool. `traffic-switch --set cpu-fallback --match non-enterprise`
support_lina: sending a note to affected customers: "We are experiencing degraded GPU capacity in us-east-1; we've applied mitigations and some traffic is routed to fallback models. Engineers are actively restoring capacity."
sre_anna: new nodes launched but kubelet failing due to taint mismatch: nodes carry taint `node.kubernetes.io/gpu-provisioning=true:NoSchedule`. cluster-autoscaler should tolerate but our admission webhook rejects new nodes without `node-role.kubernetes.io/gpu=true` label.
ml_oncall_ree: can we relax webhook for health window? if so we can let nodes join then patch labels. engops_jay?
engops_jay: we can patch webhook rules but that's risky. Alternative: run a bootstrap job to label nodes after they appear, but they never appear as schedulable. I can temporarily add `--ignore-taints` flag to the autoscaler? there's no such simple flag.
sre_anna: quick workaround: create a DaemonSet that runs on all provisioning nodes by matching a nodeSelector on the instance metadata (aws node-name pattern). It will run a job on node join that sets the label and removes the taint.
ml_oncall_ree: go for it, small script only.
engops_jay: deploying small bootstrap DaemonSet now: ```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: gpu-bootstrap
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      name: gpu-bootstrap
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        name: gpu-bootstrap
    spec:
      tolerations:
      - key: "node.kubernetes.io/gpu-provisioning"
        operator: "Exists"
        effect: "NoSchedule"
      containers:
      - name: bootstrap
        image: alpine:3.18
        command: ["/bin/sh","-c","kubectl label node $(hostname) node-role.kubernetes.io/gpu=true --overwrite && kubectl taint nodes $(hostname) node.kubernetes.io/gpu-provisioning:NoSchedule- || true"]
```
infra-bot: DaemonSet gpu-bootstrap created in namespace kube-system.
sre_anna: nodes are now transitioning to Ready and showing label role/gpu=true. kube-scheduler allowing pods.
ml_oncall_ree: queue length dropping from 11.2k -> 2.4k over 6 minutes. Throttled requests reduced.
support_lina: updating customer comms: "Most customers have traffic restored; a minority may see results routed to fallback models; we'll follow up with incident summary."
product_tom: good. any ETA to full recovery?
sre_anna: monitoring, but autoscaler still has stale LT v7 references. Need a follow-up change to rollback the LT rollout and ensure the launch-template validator has a dry-run test.
ml_oncall_ree: immediate mitigations done: manual ASG switch, bootstrap DaemonSet to label nodes, traffic routing fallback. Marking P1 -> P1 degraded moving to mitigation.
sre_anna: I'll open an infra ticket to revert launch template rollout and add preflight checks to our CI.
engops_jay: pushed change to ASG config to pin LT v6 until rollout is fixed.
ml_oncall_ree: handoff — I'm going to sleep in 25m; @sre_anna will take on-call for next hour.
sre_anna: taking over. I'll keep watch for 2 hours.
support_lina: final quick numbers: ~420k tokens attempted during spike, ~3.1% resulted in 503s, ~12 enterprise customers reported issues, we've already reached out.
product_tom: thanks all. post-incident: need RCA on LT rollout gating + add synthetic GPU pool test.
ml_oncall_ree: agreed. adding postmortem action items in incident tracker. :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated — capacity restored, autoscaler pinned. Please file postmortem and tag infra/eng-sre/engops.
infra-bot: ticket created: INFRA-3251 "rollback launch-template v7 and add preflight tests"
ml_oncall_ree: closing thread for now. if anything new pings me directly. :thumbsup:
